research_data.mission_values: Suncorp Group is undergoing significant digital transformation following the sale of its insurance arm to Allianz, refocusing on banking. The Digital Experience team is charged with reimagining customer interactions across all digital channels. The company emphasizes customer focus, quality delivery, and a collaborative culture where designers work seamlessly with cross-functional teams. Values include inclusive design practices, evidence-based decision-making over opinion, and psychological safety within teams.
research_data.culture_overview: The design culture at Suncorp emphasizes cross-functional integration with Product Managers, Developers, UX Researchers, and Content Strategists working closely together. Regular design critique sessions promote constructive dialogue and shared learning, with strong knowledge-sharing practices where team members elevate collective design capability. The environment balances individual design craft with collaborative team effort, embedding designers within Agile squads for daily stand-ups, sprint planning, and retrospectives. As a large financial institution, there is established emphasis on compliance and security, requiring designers to balance user experience with regulatory requirements and business needs. The team operates with a user-centric mindset and data-informed design approach, valuing portfolios that demonstrate measurable impact and product thinking.

Operating within established processes and legacy systems typical of large financial institutions while driving modern design practices
Managing complexity of regulated-industry design requiring understanding of privacy laws, credit checks, and financial services compliance frameworks
research_data.strategic_plan: Suncorp is executing a focused banking strategy following divestment of insurance operations, with digital transformation as a core pillar. The Digital Experience — Banking & Wealth unit is central to this vision, building modern web and mobile experiences for over 1.8 million banking customers. Strategic priorities include scaling the Figma-based 'Spark' design system across product teams, embedding accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) and inclusive design as standard practice, leveraging GenAI solutions recognized by industry awards, and expanding design capabilities through hybrid teams in Brisbane and Melbourne. The focus is on evidence-based, data-informed design using analytics platforms like Amplitude and Google Analytics to validate hypotheses and drive measurable customer outcomes, positioning Suncorp as a digitally competitive banking-focused institution.
research_data.interview_focus: Suncorp's interview process for UX/UI designers is thorough and multi-stage, averaging around 20 days. Candidates should expect an initial HR screening discussing background and software proficiency, followed by hiring manager conversations about design background and career goals. The core technical evaluation centers on a comprehensive portfolio review presentation where candidates present diverse project types to a panel including designers and product team members — the portfolio must demonstrate end-to-end process from research through ideation, testing, and iteration, not just final screens. Interviewers assess collaboration style, stakeholder communication abilities, ability to articulate design rationale to technical and non-technical audiences including senior leadership (GM level), and demonstrated user-centered design thinking with measurable impact. Technical skills in Figma (components, auto layout, Dev Mode), user research capabilities (planning and conducting studies independently), and accessibility knowledge (WCAG 2.1 AA) are heavily scrutinized. Strong emphasis on evaluating cultural fit including constructive feedback handling, cross-functional teamwork within Agile squads, and alignment with Suncorp's values around customer focus, quality, and evidence over opinion. Prior experience in financial services or regulated industries is highly regarded but not essential — the hiring team values strong design methodology and problem-solving abilities as transferable skills.
research_data.hiring_unit_intelligence: The Digital Experience — Banking & Wealth unit is the specialized design and product team within Suncorp Group responsible for all digital customer touchpoints across banking products. This unit is leading the company's post-divestment digital transformation, positioned strategically to reimagine experiences for 1.8 million banking customers across web, native mobile (iOS/Android), and emerging channels. The unit operates cross-functional Agile squads embedding designers with Product Managers, Engineers, Data Analysts, and Content Designers. Leadership includes Design Leads overseeing squad work, with the team distributed across Brisbane and Melbourne in hybrid arrangements (3 days in-office). The unit maintains and evolves the 'Spark' design system built in Figma, with regular cross-squad design critiques and knowledge-sharing sessions fostering a collaborative learning culture. Recent LinkedIn profiles show the unit employs Senior UX Designers and Senior Product Designers including noted individuals like Nick Li, Voravan Atikomtrirat, and David Tran, indicating an established mid-to-senior design capability. The unit emphasizes data-informed design using analytics platforms (Amplitude, Google Analytics) and has been recognized with the AFR AI Builder award for GenAI solutions, signaling innovation in emerging technologies. The culture within the unit prioritizes psychological safety, mentorship of junior designers, and balancing individual craft with team outcomes. Reports-to structure indicates Design Leads managing individual contributors at Senior Band level, with pathways for progression into lead and principal roles.
